product: Defence and security systems: Gripen fighters (Aeronautics), RBS 70 NG air defence and weapons (Dynamics), GlobalEye AEW&C plus sensors and command and control (Surveillance), and A26 submarines under the new Naval business area. Headquartered in Linkoping, Sweden, with about 29,000 employees.
demand: High. CEO Micael Johansson says demand for the product offering remains high as customers invest in both immediate and long-term needs. Q2 2026 order bookings were SEK 68,393m versus SEK 28,403m a year earlier, a 2.7x book-to-bill, with continued capacity expansion to meet demand.
pricing_power: Not directly evidenced. Growth is described as organic volume from demand (29.8 percent organic sales growth in Q2 2026) rather than price. Q2 EBIT margin was 11.0 percent versus 10.0 percent a year earlier and EBITDA margin 14.8 percent versus 14.3 percent. No pricing commentary found in sources read.
competition: Western defence primes. Evidence read: Airbus pitching Eurofighter to Portugal, and analysts framing Saab as a European defence-boom winner (BofA, 2026-09-21). Saab competes in fighters, AEW&C and air defence, but named competitor comparisons were not detailed in primary sources read (aggregator context only).
team: CEO and President Micael Johansson; CFO Anna Wijkander; Head of Investor Relations Johan Andersson. From 2026-10-01: Anders Carp heads Dynamics and stays deputy CEO; Marcus Wandt heads Aeronautics; Lars Tossman heads Group Strategy and Growth; Gorgen Johansson becomes strategic advisor. Announced 2026-09-10 to support growth and innovation.
market_strategy: Act as a system integrator and expand capacity to meet demand. Saab established a new Naval business area from Q2 2026, signed space-domain MoUs with SSC Space, OHB Sweden and Ericsson (2026-09-24), and focuses investment on five core areas with continued capacity expansion, deliveries and innovation.
bull: Q2 2026 order bookings SEK 68,393m vs 28,403m, book-to-bill 2.7x, organic sales +29.8%, EBIT margin 11.0% vs 10.0%, backlog SEK 274.5bn; Poland A26 submarines ~SEK 47bn (2026-06-29).
bear: Q2 operational cash flow -SEK 62m, net liquidity fell to SEK 2,523m from SEK 3,989m; consensus Hold, mean target 629.21 vs price 615.50; UBS and SEB cut targets; GlobalEye Netherlands only an LOI.
falsifier: Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-23 showing order bookings below SEK 28,403m or another negative quarterly operating cash flow.
web_what_changed: 2026-06-29 Poland ordered three A26 submarines approx SEK 47bn. Q2 2026 (2026-07-17): order bookings SEK 68,393m vs 28,403m, sales SEK 25,453m up 29.8 percent organic, EBIT SEK 2,794m, new Naval business area. Also Finland RBS 70 NG order SEK 1.2bn, Netherlands GlobalEye LOI, Gripen F first flight, space MoUs, group management changes from 2026-10-01.
web_not_known_yesterday: No company disclosure dated 2026-09-25 was found. Newest items are 2026-09-24: MoUs with SSC Space, OHB Sweden and Ericsson for a broader space-domain system-integrator role, plus the Nomination Committee for the 2027 AGM. Aggregator note: Barclays raised its Saab target to 755 SEK on 2026-09-21.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Demand and volume, not price. Q2 2026 organic sales growth was 29.8 percent with order bookings SEK 68,393m and book-to-bill 2.7x; the CEO cites high customer demand and capacity expansion. Mix shifted with the new Naval business area (Poland submarines). No price-led growth was disclosed in sources read.
web_suppliers: Not found. Saab does not name key suppliers in the sources read; it states it develops products in cooperation with suppliers worldwide and qualifies them through an assessment process using Ivalua. No supplier constraint was disclosed. SSC Space, OHB Sweden and Ericsson are cooperation MoUs, not confirmed suppliers.
web_customers: Governments and defence authorities, highly concentrated. Named in the last 90 days: Sweden FMV, Polish State Treasury Armaments Agency, Finnish Defence Forces Logistics Command, the Netherlands, and Bulgarian air navigation service BULATSA. Backlog was SEK 274,532m at end-2025. No customer revenue split was disclosed in sources read.
web_who_loses: Rival Western defence primes competing for the same European and NATO budgets. Evidence read: Airbus is pitching Eurofighter to Portugal as an F-16 replacement, and analysts call Saab a defence-boom winner (BofA, 2026-09-21). Named loser specifics beyond the Eurofighter coalition were not confirmed in primary sources (aggregator context only).
web_contradicting_evidence: Valuation, cash and unbooked demand. Price 615.50 SEK versus consensus mean 629.21 SEK (only about +2 percent); consensus rating Hold; low target 330 SEK, about -46 percent. Recent cuts: UBS 780 to 760, SEB 634 to 619. Q2 operational cash flow was negative SEK 62m and net liquidity fell to SEK 2,523m from SEK 3,989m at end-2025. Netherlands GlobalEye is only an LOI, no order received.
web_if_management_right: Record order bookings (SEK 68,393m in Q2 2026, book-to-bill 2.7x) plus capacity expansion convert into years of elevated organic growth with rising margins, supported by the SEK 274.5bn backlog at end-2025 and deliveries such as the Polish submarines running to 2038.
web_if_management_wrong: Cash and execution break first: negative Q2 operational cash flow and lower net liquidity while ramping capacity, with margin pressure if ramp and supply costs bite. Second break point is dependence on government budgets and on converting non-binding intentions such as the Netherlands GlobalEye LOI into firm orders.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Swedish and Nordic suppliers, subcontractors and space partners. Evidence read: MoUs with SSC Space, OHB Sweden and Ericsson (2026-09-24) for a space system-integrator role. Broader second-order suppliers were not named in sources read; aggregator coverage points to European defence supply chains generally.
